restaurants.name: Desi Dastarkhwan
restaurants.address: Shop 14, Jinnah Super Market, F-7 Markaz, Islamabad
restaurants.description: A family-run desi kitchen in Jinnah Super, F-7, best known for its dum-cooked chicken and mutton biryani made in a sealed degh every few hours. The menu sticks to home-style classics: overnight beef nihari, karahi, palak paneer and a light yellow daal for weekday lunches. items.name: Beef Nihari

items.name: Chicken Karahi (Half)

items.name: Palak Paneer

items.name: Paneer Makhani

items.name: Yellow Daal Tadka

items.name: Roghni Naan (2 pcs)

items.name: Thai Peanut Tofu Salad

reviews.text: Best chicken biryani in F-7, no contest. Rice was separate and fluffy, chicken fell off the bone and the aloo bukhara gave that little tang. Ordered for office lunch and everyone asked where it was from.
Mutton was tender with no smell at all, and the masala had depth without burning your mouth. Raita was thick and cold. Came in a sealed foil tray so it was still steaming when it reached G-6.
Nihari was rich and the shank meat was melting, but it needed more ginger and lemon on the side. Naan was soft. Solid Sunday breakfast.
Zabardast biryani yaar. Proper dum flavour, not that food-colour orange stuff. Portion is enough for one hungry person or two light eaters.
Wanted something light for a weekday lunch and this hit the spot. The daal is thin and homely with a nice garlic tarka, salad was crunchy and fresh. Would be 5 stars if they sent a roti with it.
Paneer makhani is very rich, lots of butter and cream, definitely not a diet meal. Paneer cubes were soft. Garlic naan was a bit chewy by the time it arrived.
Karahi was okay, slightly too much oil floating on top and the tomatoes weren't fully cooked down. The biryani here is much better, stick to that.

I have been meaning to write this for a while because Desi Dastarkhwan has quietly become the place my whole family orders from whenever there is anything to celebrate, and the reason is simple: the chicken biryani. Let me explain why it is different from the dozen other biryanis we have tried across Islamabad.

First, the rice. Every grain is long, separate and properly cooked through, never mushy at the bottom and never hard at the top, which tells you it is genuinely dum-cooked rather than mixed together at the last minute. The layers are visible when you open the tray: white rice, saffron-yellow rice and then the masala-coated chicken sitting underneath. Second, the masala itself. It is spicy, but in a warm, rounded way; you get the green chilli and black pepper, then the fried onions and a little sourness from the dried plums. It is not the fluorescent orange, food-colour biryani that some places sell. Third, the chicken. Bone-in pieces, marinated long enough that the yoghurt has actually tenderised them, so the meat slides off the bone. On our last order for my father's retirement dinner we got twelve portions and I genuinely could not find a dry piece in any of them.

The mint raita deserves a mention too. Fresh mint, thick yoghurt, a bit of cumin, and they pack it in a separate sealed tub so it does not leak onto the rice. We also took the shahi kheer for dessert and it was a hit with the elders: creamy, not overly sweet, and generously topped with pistachio and almond slivers. If anyone in your family has a nut allergy, do note that the kheer is loaded with nuts.

Delivery to our house in F-10 took about forty minutes on a Saturday night, which is reasonable given the order size, and everything arrived hot because they use foil trays inside a thick paper bag. The rider called ahead and was polite. Pricing is fair: 690 for a single portion that easily satisfies one hungry adult.

Small suggestions: I would love an option for extra raita in the order form, and maybe a family-size biryani tray so we do not have to order twelve separate boxes. But honestly these are minor. If you live anywhere near F-7 and want reliable, flavourful, properly made biryani, this is the one to order. Highly recommended.
The kheer is thick, not too sweet, with plenty of crushed pistachio and almond. Perfect after iftar.
Ordered for iftar for 6 people. Biryani was consistent across all boxes, every piece had masala and the rice wasn't mushy. Kheer was the perfect finish. Delivery was on time even in the maghrib rush.
Palak paneer tasted homemade: smooth spinach, mild spice, not oily. Good for my vegetarian colleague who usually gets nothing at desi places.
Nihari arrived lukewarm and the oil had set on top. Flavour was fine once reheated but for 850 I expect it to arrive hot. Took 55 minutes.
Mutton biryani on a Friday is now a ritual in our house. Generous meat, about 4-5 pieces, and the rice is fragrant with kewra. Bohat acha.
I have tried most biryani places in Islamabad and this is the closest to proper Karachi-style without being overly spicy. The raita has fresh mint, not dried. Packaging is leak-proof.
Karahi had a nice ginger kick and lots of green chillies; the half portion fed two of us easily with three naans. Slightly salty but overall tasty.
Got chicken handi instead of paneer makhani, and I'm vegetarian. Called them and they offered a refund but the evening was wasted.
Honestly the most underrated thing here. Light, comforting, not greasy and very cheap. My go-to when I'm sick of heavy food.
Great biryani as always but they forgot the raita this time. Still the best rice in F-7.
Mutton biryani was good but the portion felt smaller than last time, maybe 3 pieces. Salad was fine. Price has gone up too.
Late night order at 11pm and it still came in 30 minutes. Palak paneer creamy and naan soft and buttery. Love that they're open late.
Finally a proper healthy lunch option in F-6. The quinoa bowl is light but filling, veggies were nicely charred and the lemon-tahini dressing came on the side so nothing got soggy.
Good caesar, the chicken was juicy rather than dry rubbery breast. Dressing is lighter than usual which I liked. Croutons got a bit soft in transit.
The peri peri bowl actually has heat, which is rare for a 'healthy' place. Brown rice, charred corn, pickled onions, great balance. I get this three times a week for office lunch.
Crunchy, fresh and the peanut dressing is addictive. Tofu could be crispier. Note for allergy folks: lots of peanuts in it.
Light, fresh and only 750. Hummus is smooth and the roasted peppers add sweetness. Perfect desk lunch that doesn't make you sleepy at 3pm.
Avocado toast tasted good but the poached eggs were overcooked, no runny yolk. Also 1150 is steep for two slices of toast.
Not too sweet and you can really taste the ginger. Came cold with ice packed separately. Nice touch.
Moist carrot cake loaded with walnuts and a thin cream cheese frosting. My guilty pleasure after the gym, ironically.
Paneer tikka wrap has a decent chilli kick and the mint chutney is fresh. Good spicy vegetarian option under 800.
Wrap was soggy by the time it arrived and the pesto was mostly oil. Chicken was fine. Expected better for the price.
Vegan and actually tasty. Chickpea salad with cucumber, olives, red onion and lemon is fresh and zingy, and it pairs well with the green smoothie.
Good pre-workout snack, dense and not overly sweet. A bit small for 450 though.
I'm vegan and this place is a lifesaver in Islamabad. Quinoa bowl is clean and well-seasoned. Staff even confirmed there's no dairy in the dressing when I called.
Lettuce was wilted and brown at the edges and the chicken had a sour smell. Threw it away. Very disappointing for a place that sells itself on fresh food.
Tasty and filling, the peri peri is properly hot. Portion of rice is small though, mostly chicken and veg.
Ordered for a team meeting. Wraps were neatly cut in halves and labelled. Everyone loved the carrot cake.
Sourdough was crusty, avocado seasoned with chilli flakes and lime, and the eggs were perfect this time. Weekend brunch sorted.
Flavour is nice but the dressing is very heavy on peanut, which kind of defeats the 'light salad' idea. Cabbage was crunchy at least.
Light, fresh, and keeps me full till evening. Bohat acha option for anyone on a diet.
Quick delivery, 20 minutes to F-7. Wrap was warm, smoothie cold. Good value lunch combo.
Hummus is silky smooth with good olive oil, and the moutabal is properly smoky; you can tell the aubergine was charred over flame. Pita came warm.
Tawook is juicy and garlicky, with the toum on the side. Best in F-8 hands down.
Ordered the mixed grill for a family dinner of four and there were leftovers. Kofta, tawook and lamb tikka all well grilled, rice fragrant. Worth the 4200.
Solid shawarma wrap, tightly rolled with nice pickles inside. Wish it had a bit more garlic sauce.
The harra wrap is genuinely spicy, all chilli, garlic and coriander, and it's under 800. My new late night order.
Fresh, crunchy and tangy from the sumac and pomegranate molasses. Pita chips stayed crisp because they packed them separately. Great light lunch.
Falafel were crispy outside but a bit dry and dense inside. Tahini sauce helped. The hummus here is better.
Kofta is well spiced with that seven-spice warmth, not chilli hot. A little greasy but tasty.
Flaky, syrupy and packed with pistachio. Better than what I had in Dubai, honestly.

We hosted a small office celebration at home for eight people last week and decided to go Lebanese instead of the usual BBQ, so I ordered two mixed grill platters, a couple of mezze and a box of baklava from Cedar & Charcoal in F-8. I was nervous because Middle Eastern food in Islamabad is often just shawarma with a different name, but this turned out to be the highlight of the evening.

The mixed grill platter is genuinely built for sharing. Each one had shish tawook, lamb kofta, lamb tikka, grilled tomatoes and onions, a big bed of vermicelli rice, hummus and two tubs of garlic toum. The tawook was marinated in yoghurt and lemon and stayed juicy, the kofta had that warm seven-spice flavour with plenty of parsley, and the lamb tikka was tender with a light char. Nothing was chilli-hot, which made it easy for everyone, including the kids. For people who want heat, they included a small pot of chilli paste when I asked in the order notes.

The moutabal was the surprise. It is properly smoky, the aubergine has clearly been charred over an open flame, and it is blended with tahini, garlic and a squeeze of lemon, finished with pomegranate seeds. Scooped up with the warm pita, it disappeared before the grills were even opened. We also had fattoush, which stayed crisp because the pita chips and dressing were packed separately.

Dessert was the pistachio baklava: flaky layers, not soggy, sweet syrup and an honest amount of pistachio. A guest who has lived in Amman said it reminded her of the real thing.

Delivery took about 45 minutes for a big order, the food arrived hot, and the platters came in sturdy compartment trays with nothing leaking. Two platters at 4200 each plus mezze came to just over 11,000 rupees for eight adults, which I thought was very fair given the quality and the amount left over.

My only wish is that they offered a vegetarian platter version, since we had one vegetarian guest who survived on mezze and falafel. Otherwise, a perfect evening and I will be ordering the platter again for Eid.
Halloumi was squeaky and salty in the good way; mint and tomato balance it. Great vegetarian wrap.
Shawarma plate arrived cold and the fries were soggy. Chicken was fine but overall disappointing for 1250.
Batata harra is dangerously addictive: crispy potato cubes, garlic, chilli and lots of coriander. Good spicy snack and vegan too.
My vegan friend and I shared moutabal and fattoush. Fresh, light and full of flavour; the moutabal had a lovely smoky depth.
Consistent every time. Tawook could use a bit more char but the hummus is perfect.
Platter was missing the kofta and the rice was undercooked and hard. Called them and they said they'd fix it next time. Not acceptable at 4200.
Cheap and cheerful combo. Wrap was hot, potatoes crispy. Delivered to E-11 in 30 mins.
Too spicy for me honestly, I couldn't taste anything but chilli. If you love heat you'll enjoy it.
Baklava a bit too sweet for my taste but fresh. Hummus great as always.
Kofta and fattoush made a perfect balanced dinner. Meat juicy, salad bright. Zabardast.
Biryani was dry as sawdust, the rice at the bottom was hard and there was barely any masala. Huge portion though, which just means more dry rice.
Grand BBQ platter could feed six people, not four. Tikka, seekh and malai boti all smoky and fresh off the coals. Unbeatable for a family dinner.
Seekh kebabs are juicy and spicy with that charcoal smoke. Four huge kebabs for under 800 is a steal.
Malai boti melts in the mouth, creamy and mild. Perfect for kids who can't handle spice.
Tikka was great, smoky and well marinated. Biryani was dry again and under-spiced, needed a whole tub of raita. Stick to BBQ here.

Writing a detailed review because Al-Markaz Tikka House is both one of my favourite and most frustrating places in G-9, and new customers should know what to order and what to skip.

First, the portions. They are enormous. The Grand BBQ Platter says it feeds four to five, but we were six adults and still packed leftovers for the next day. You get chicken tikka, beef seekh kebabs, malai boti, reshmi kebab, wings, four naans, raita and a sharp green chutney. Everything comes straight off the coals and you can taste the smoke. The seekh kebabs are especially good, juicy and well-spiced with a proper chilli kick, and the malai boti is creamy and mild, which kept the kids happy. At 4400 rupees it is some of the best value-for-money BBQ in Islamabad.

Now the problem: the chicken biryani. I have ordered it four times over the last few months hoping it would improve, and every time the rice has been dry. Not slightly dry, the kind of dry where the bottom layer is almost crunchy and there is no masala clinging to the grains. The chicken pieces are large, which is consistent with their huge-portion style, but they sit on top of plain-looking rice instead of being layered through it. It feels like the biryani is made early in the day and reheated. If you want rice from here, order the chicken pulao instead. The pulao is moist, cooked in a proper yakhni, fragrant with whole spices and black pepper, and the portion again is massive, honestly enough for two.

Delivery is usually 40 to 50 minutes on weekends, a bit slower on Friday nights, but everything arrives hot in foil trays with the naan wrapped separately so it does not sweat. The riders know the sectors well and have never got lost finding our street in G-10.

So, my advice: come here for the BBQ, the pulao, the mutton champ and the karahi, and you will be very happy with the quantity and the taste. Skip the biryani unless they fix it; for biryani in this part of town, the places in F-7 are much better. Four stars because the grill section alone earns it.
Full mutton karahi served four of us with plenty left over. Meat was tender, gravy thick with tomato and ginger.
Bihari boti has proper coal smoke and heat. A bit chewy in places but the flavour is excellent.
Pulao is much better than their biryani: moist, aromatic, with real yakhni flavour. Portion is massive.
The champ is the star here. Thick chops, charred edges, spicy marinade. Bohat zabardast.
Daal makhani is heavy and buttery, real comfort food and not light at all. Paratha flaky. One portion was enough for two.
Dry, bland biryani and the chicken piece was tiny despite the 'double portion' claim. Also arrived 50 minutes late. Never again.
Late night tikka paratha craving solved. Tikka was juicy and still hot. Huge leg piece.
Massive amount of food for the price. Reshmi kebabs were a bit salty but everything else was spot on.
Aloo palak was okay but very oily. Not many vegetarian choices here, it's really a meat place.
Ordered for a cricket match get-together; the seekh and malai boti disappeared in minutes. Packaging kept everything hot.
Rice was dry and clumpy, like it had been reheated. Their BBQ is great but whoever makes the biryani needs to try again.
Champ and daal makhani with naan: heaviest meal of my life and I regret nothing. Portions are huge.
Good food, big portions. Bihari boti was smoky and hot, pulao fragrant. Delivery a bit slow on a Friday night.
450 for a tikka this size is unreal value. Charred, juicy, spicy. My regular.
Green curry was creamy and fragrant with real Thai basil. But it took 75 minutes to arrive. Food great, delivery painfully slow.
Tom yum is fiery and sour, exactly like Bangkok. Prawns were plump. Worth the wait, and there is always a wait.
Tasty pad thai with good tamarind balance, but it took over an hour and the noodles had clumped together.
Spicy basil noodles are seriously hot, bird's eye chillies everywhere. Loved it. Ordered at 7, ate at 8:10 though.
Spring rolls were soggy and limp after a 70 minute delivery. Probably great fresh from the fryer.

I really want to love Wok & Basil, and on the food alone I would give it five stars, but after more than a dozen orders I have to be honest about the delivery times, because they are consistently the slowest of any restaurant I order from in Islamabad.

Let me start with the good. The Thai green curry is excellent: creamy coconut base, real Thai basil and kaffir lime leaves, tender chicken thigh, aubergine and bamboo shoots, and a heat level that builds slowly rather than hitting you all at once. The tom yum soup with prawns is the most authentic I have found in Pakistan, sour and fiery and full of lemongrass and galangal, with properly plump prawns. The pad thai has a good balance of tamarind sweetness and sourness, with crushed peanuts and lime on the side. The kitchen clearly knows what it is doing.

Now the bad. Out of my last twelve orders, only two arrived within an hour. Most land between 65 and 80 minutes, and once it took one hour and forty minutes. It does not seem to matter whether I order at lunch from my office in Blue Area, which is practically next door, or at dinner from home in G-11. The app estimate always says 35 minutes and the actual time is double. When I called once, the person said they cook everything fresh to order and the kitchen is small, which I respect, but then the estimate should be honest.

The long wait affects the food. The pad thai noodles clump together after an hour in a box, and spring rolls that are crispy in the restaurant become limp. Curries and soups survive better, though once the tom yum lid was not sealed properly and a third of it was in the bag.

My workaround now is to place the order 90 minutes before I actually want to eat, or to pick it up myself, which takes about 25 minutes from ordering. If you plan ahead, the food is worth it. If you are hungry right now, order somewhere else.

Three stars: five for the cooking, one for the delivery experience. Please fix the timing, Wok & Basil, because you could easily be the best Asian place in the city.
Massaman is mild, rich and the beef falls apart. Peanuts and potato make it hearty. Great for people who don't like heat.

items: Thai Basil Chicken Rice Bowl (Pad Krapow)
reviews.text: Pad krapow with the fried egg on top is my favourite comfort food. Very spicy. Delivery slow as usual, 60 minutes.
Satay was tender and the peanut sauce rich. Bit pricey for 4 skewers.
One of the few proper vegan curries in Islamabad. Red curry is spicy and creamy from the coconut, and the tofu soaks it up. Order early because they are slow.
Tom kha is soothing, coconutty and only mildly spicy. Perfect for a rainy evening.
Order took 1 hour 40 minutes and arrived cold. Rice was hard. Called twice, nobody picked up. Food might be good but the service is terrible.
Mango sticky rice is heavenly: sweet ripe mango, salty coconut cream, chewy rice. Only available in mango season so grab it.
Ordered for an office lunch in Blue Area; placed the order at 12 to get it by 1:15. Food was excellent, especially the satay.
Way too oily this time and the noodles were broken. Spice level still good though.
Soup spilled in the bag because the lid wasn't sealed, and the delivery took forever. Half a soup for 990.
Best massaman in town. Slow cooked, deep flavour.
Lovely vegan dinner. Only complaint is the wait, 65 minutes to F-10.

items: Thai Basil Chicken Rice Bowl (Pad Krapow)
reviews.text: Pad krapow zabardast, proper heat and crispy egg edges. Picked it up myself to skip the delivery wait, which is the only way to go with this place.
Curry was watery and too sweet compared to before. Plus the usual 70 min delivery.
Proper Karachi biryani with aloo and lots of masala. Spicy enough to make my nose run. Chicken was tender.
Light and fresh veggie wrap, grilled peppers and crunchy slaw with mint chutney. Good quick lunch.
Haleem is thick and stringy, just how it should be. Came with fried onions, ginger, lemon and chaat masala on the side.
Karahi was tasty, tomatoey and full of green chilli. Half portion was enough for two. A bit oily.
Qorma was decent but very oily and the almond flavour was faint. Average.
Chapli kebabs are huge with crispy edges, studded with tomato and pomegranate seeds. Spicy and juicy.
Good roll for 450; paratha was flaky and the chutney had a kick. Bit small.
Daal chawal like ghar ka khana. Light, comforting, with achaar on the side. Under 500 too.
Soft, warm gulab jamun, not too syrupy. Nice end to the meal.
Biryani was too salty this time and the raita was missing. Usually it's good, so hoping it was a one-off.
Winter special gajar ka halwa with khoya and almonds. Rich and comforting.
Boti was smoky and well marinated. Good with naan and chutney.
Two light vegetarian lunches that don't feel like a compromise. Wrap was fresh, daal well tempered.
Office ordered 15 biryanis for a farewell lunch and all arrived hot in 35 minutes. Consistent spice level across boxes. Zabardast.
Good food, slightly late delivery to Clifton, about 50 mins.
Karahi was mostly oil and bones. Very little meat. Not worth 1400.
Late night BBQ fix. Everything hot and smoky. Fast delivery even at 1am.
Wrap was a bit bland and needed more chutney. Healthy though.
Qorma this time was excellent: rich, aromatic, mild spice. Family dinner hit.
Spicy, flavourful biryani with a good amount of aloo. Rice a little broken, but the taste is great.
Classic Karachi bun kebab: egg-dipped shami, chutney, onions, soft bun. Tastes like Boat Basin at midnight. Only 280!
Chatni roll is fire, literally. Green chutney and chilli boti with garlic mayo to calm it down. Best cheap spicy food in Clifton.
Full karahi was huge and very spicy, lots of green chilli and black pepper. Oil heavy, but that's street karahi for you.
Gola kebabs are soft, smoky and melt in your mouth. Spicy, under 800, and the onion rings with lemon are perfect.
Dahi baray were soft and the yoghurt cold and sweet-tangy. Great iftar item.
Iftar sorted. Chana chaat tangy and fresh, samosas crispy with spicy potato filling.

Every Karachiite has a list of street food spots they swear by, and since moving back to Clifton this kitchen has gone to the top of mine. It captures the feel of eating at Boat Basin at midnight, but delivered to your door, which with a newborn at home is exactly what we needed.

Start with the anda shami bun kebab. It is the real thing: a soft, slightly sweet bun toasted on the tawa with butter, a shami patty made with beef and chana daal, dipped in beaten egg and fried until the edges are lacy, then layered with green chutney, imli chutney, raw onion rings and shredded cabbage. It is spicy, tangy, messy and costs 280 rupees. They wrap each one in butter paper and foil so it holds together. I have ordered these at least ten times and they have never been cold.

The gola kebab plate is the dish I would send anyone to try first. The kebabs are so soft they barely hold their shape, heavily spiced with red chilli and smoky from the coal, served with onion rings, lemon wedges and mint chutney. At 750 rupees it is one of the best spicy dishes under 800 in Clifton. Be warned that the heat level is genuinely high; my brother-in-law from Lahore needed a glass of lassi to recover.

For a weekend family dinner we ordered the full chicken karahi, which served four of us with parathas from home. It is a proper street-style karahi: chicken cooked hard in a wok with tomatoes, loads of green chillies, ginger julienne and crushed black pepper. It is oily, I won't pretend otherwise, but the flavour is excellent and the chicken was tender. If you want something gentler, the white karahi is creamy and much milder.

Delivery is fast, usually 25 to 35 minutes to Block 4, and the riders are friendly. Packaging is better than most street places: sealed karahi containers, chutneys in separate pots, no leaks.

Only gripe is that late at night they sometimes run out of gola kebabs, so order before 11. Otherwise, zabardast in every sense. Five stars.

items: Double Shami Bun Kebab with Cheese
reviews.text: Cheese felt unnecessary and the bun was soggy from the chutney. Stick with the original anda shami.
White karahi is creamy with crushed black pepper and very mild. Great for people who can't handle the regular karahi heat.
Bihari roll is smoky, tender and very spicy. Paratha crispy. Late night favourite after a Do Darya drive.
Peshawari karahi is simple, just mutton, salt, tomato and black pepper, and that's the beauty of it. Meat was tender.
Proper kadak doodh patti, came in a sealed cup still hot. 150 rupees of happiness.
Roll was very spicy and the lassi saved me. Lassi was thick with pistachio on top.
Bun kebab arrived squashed and cold, and the chutney had soaked through the bun. Not the same as eating it at the stall.
Samosas were okay but greasy. Chutney was good.
Wrong order: they sent white karahi instead of the regular one and it took 70 minutes. Too oily as well.
Smoky meat heaven. Gola kebabs were incredibly soft. Bohat acha.
Light and tangy snack, good for a quick evening bite. Could use more imli.
Vegetarian street food done right. Fresh cold yoghurt, crisp onions, tangy chutneys.

items: Double Shami Bun Kebab with Cheese
reviews.text: Good midnight snack combo. Bun kebab was filling and the chai was kadak.
Real Neapolitan-style margherita: leopard-spotted crust, fresh basil, milky fior di latte. Best pizza in DHA.
Diavola has proper chilli oil heat and crispy pepperoni cups. Spicy pizza lovers, this is it.
Desi tikka on a wood-fired base works surprisingly well. Spicy but not overwhelming.
Alfredo is very creamy and heavy with generous parmesan. Chicken grilled nicely. Not a light lunch.
Cheesiest mac and cheese in Karachi, crispy breadcrumb top and gooey inside. Pure comfort.
Arrabbiata has a good chilli kick and plenty of garlic. Nice that it's vegan.
As a coeliac I rarely trust restaurants, but they confirmed separate cooking. The primavera is light and fresh with olive oil and seasonal veg.
Very rich, and the gorgonzola overpowered everything. Crust was soggy in the middle by the time it arrived.

Forno Rosso is the pizza place we keep returning to in DHA Phase 6, and after maybe twenty orders across a year I think I can give a fair picture of what is great and what is just fine.

The margherita is the benchmark and it is excellent. The dough is clearly fermented for a long time; the crust is airy, chewy and blistered with those little charred leopard spots you only get from a very hot wood-fired oven. The tomato sauce is bright and simple, the fior di latte melts into creamy pools, and the basil is fresh rather than dried. It is a light pizza by Karachi standards, which I love, and a 12-inch is enough for one hungry person or two with a salad.

The four cheese pizza is the opposite: rich, heavy and very indulgent, with mozzarella, gorgonzola, parmesan and cheddar. When it arrives quickly it is a treat, but it does not travel well. Twice the centre has become soggy because the oil from all that cheese pools in the middle, and the gorgonzola can overpower everything if you are not a blue cheese fan. I would recommend it for dining in more than delivery.

The penne arrabbiata is my weeknight favourite. It is vegan, which surprised me, and has a real chilli kick from dried chilli flakes and garlic sauteed in olive oil, with a slow-cooked tomato sauce. It reheats well the next day too. For those who need it, the gluten-free penne primavera is a genuinely good option and they do take cross-contamination seriously.

On service: delivery to Clifton usually takes 35 to 45 minutes. Pizzas come in an insulated bag and are usually hot, though on busy Friday and Saturday nights I have had waits of over an hour. Prices are on the higher side, 1450 for a margherita and nearly 2000 for the specialty pizzas, but the quality justifies it compared to the chains.

Four stars overall. Five for the margherita and arrabbiata, three for the heavier pizzas on delivery, and a small deduction for weekend delays. If you only order one thing, make it the margherita.
Peppery rocket, sweet pear and candied walnuts. Fresh and light starter.
Tiramisu is light, coffee-soaked and not too sweet. Came in a neat glass jar.
Bolognese sauce was watery and the spaghetti overcooked. Not worth 1450.
Garlic bread cheesy and crisp, arrabbiata spicy. Great value dinner for two.
Nice pesto base with roasted veg. Heads up: the pesto has pine nuts, careful if you're allergic.
Birthday dinner at home: pizza arrived hot in an insulated bag and the tiramisu cold. Thoughtful packaging.
Pizza arrived 80 minutes late, cold and stuck to the box. Refund took a week.
Heavy carb overload but delicious. Alfredo sauce was silky.
Ordered for a Friday night with friends and it disappeared instantly. Spicy and loaded with toppings.
Mac and cheese was too salty and the sauce had split, with an oily layer on top.
Light, healthy Italian meal that left me feeling good. Vegetables tasted fresh.
Thick, eggy chicken corn soup like the old Chinese places. Perfect for a winter evening with chilli vinegar.
Chilli chicken dry is fiery and wok-smoky with crunchy capsicum. Ask for extra green chillies.
Classic Pakistani-Chinese combo; manchurian tangy and sweet. Rice a bit greasy.
Crispy chicken in spicy mayo, addictive. Gets soggy if you don't eat it fast.
Hot and sour was more sour than hot, and too much cornflour. Just okay.
Family combo is great value. Soup for four, manchurian, chilli chicken, rice and chowmein fed five of us.

Golden Dragon is the kind of Pakistani-Chinese restaurant that every neighbourhood in Karachi used to have in the nineties, and it has kept that style alive in Gulshan-e-Iqbal. If you are looking for authentic Cantonese or Sichuan food, this is not it. If you want the comforting, saucy, chilli-loaded Chinese that Pakistani families grew up with, it is one of the best around.

We order the Family Combo for Four almost every month for family dinner. You get four bowls of chicken corn soup, chicken manchurian, chilli chicken, egg fried rice and chicken chowmein. For 3900 rupees it fed five of us with leftovers, which makes it some of the best value in the area. The chicken corn soup is thick, eggy and mild, exactly like it should be, and they send chilli vinegar, soy sauce and chilli sauce sachets so everyone can adjust it. My kids drink it like a milkshake.

The chilli chicken dry is the dish that keeps me coming back on my own. Strips of chicken are coated, fried and then wok-tossed with sliced green chillies, onions, capsicum and soy, with real smoky wok flavour. It is properly hot, a solid three out of three on spice, and the capsicum stays crunchy. Paired with the egg fried rice it is a perfect late-night meal.

Not everything is consistent. The manchurian is sometimes very sweet and ketchup-heavy, and once the chowmein arrived soggy and lukewarm. On one combo order the chilli chicken was missing most of its green chillies, which made it oddly bland. Delivery to our block in Gulshan normally takes 30 to 40 minutes, but on rainy days or on Sunday nights it can stretch to an hour.

Packaging is decent: soups are in sealed containers inside a separate bag, and the dry dishes come in foil boxes so they don't sweat too much. Vegetarians have limited choices, but the Szechuan vegetables with tofu are genuinely spicy and well made, and they are vegan.

Overall four stars. Order the soup, the chilli chicken dry and the kung pao, ask for extra green chillies, and you will be happy.
Kung pao with roasted peanuts and dried red chillies. Good heat and crunch.
Beef chilli dry is super spicy and tender. My go-to.
Veg chowmein was bland and oily. Needed soy and chilli sauce to make it edible.
A rare vegan option in Gulshan that's actually spicy. The Szechuan peppercorns tingle and the tofu is firm.
Chowmein was soggy and cold on arrival. Took 60 minutes for a 3 km distance.
Crispy spring rolls with a good chicken and cabbage filling.
Order this every Friday. Consistent taste for years.
Manchurian was swimming in a sweet, ketchup-like sauce with too much food colour. Disappointing.
Office lunch for 8: all good, came in 30 minutes, packaging neat.
Good combo but the chilli chicken was missing green chillies. Still a huge amount of food.
Spicy, nutty kung pao and fluffy egg fried rice. Zabardast combo.
Beef was chewy and way too salty this time.
Good comfort soup and rolls on a rainy Karachi day.
Sunday halwa puri done right. Puris crispy and puffed, halwa soft and not too sweet, chanay spicy.
Nihari is spicy and thick, and the khameeri roti soft and slightly sweet. Breakfast of champions.
Paye was sticky and rich, perfect with naan. Bit too much oil for my taste.
Pink chai with crushed pistachios and almonds, creamy and fragrant. Lovely.
Masala omelette with onion, tomato and green chilli, and the paratha was flaky. Simple and filling.
Aloo paratha was heavy and greasy, though filling. Dahi was fresh.
Puris arrived soggy and cold and the halwa had become a lump. Halwa puri doesn't travel well, better to eat in.
Rabri falooda is thick and creamy with vermicelli, basil seeds and crushed pistachios. A summer must.
Spicy chickpeas, good with puri. Vegan friendly too.
Strong doodh patti, just right.
Suji halwa with almonds and cardamom, rich in ghee. Better than my nani's (don't tell her).
Kheer in a clay pot has that earthy flavour, pistachio on top. Lovely.
Nihari was too salty and oily this time.
Family breakfast for 6, everything hot and delivered by 9am. Bohat acha.
Good cheap breakfast. Puris a bit oily.
Paye had a strong smell and wasn't cleaned properly. Couldn't eat it.
Perfect quick breakfast before office. Fast delivery in the Tariq Road area.
Hearty breakfast with a generous paratha. Chai a bit too sweet.
Nihari has a good spicy kick and tender beef, under 800 for a full bowl. Great value.
Falooda had melted and leaked in the bag. Kheer was fine.

review.text: Biryani spicy exactly how I like it, aloo perfectly soft, and the tikka boti had great char. Reached Clifton hot in 35 minutes.
Karahi had serious heat and the gola kebabs were smoky and soft. A bit oily, but exactly the desi fix I wanted.
Chilli chicken dry with extra green chillies was perfect. Rice slightly greasy, and it took 50 minutes from Gulshan to Clifton.
Rolls for a late night match with friends. Bihari roll smoky and fiery, chatni roll properly spicy. Zabardast.
Tikka pizza was good and spicy, but the bolognese was bland and watery.
